newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediobanca shares fluctuate in Milan.
newsitem.headline: Mediobanca shares fluctuate in Milan.

text.p: Shares in secretive Italian merchant bank Mediobanca wavered on the Milan stock market on Monday, at one point dipping two percent as dealers digested newspaper reports of discord at the powerful bank.

Following newspaper reports at the weekend that central director Gerardo Braggiotti was quitting the Milan bank, dealers were watching for further developments and speculating over a possible shift in power behind closed doors.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported that Braggiotti, 45, seen as a young star at the bank, was on the point of leaving due to a disagreement with top management over strategy.
Newspapers said however his departure had not yet been formalised. No one at Mediobanca was available for comment.
"There seems to be some kind of power struggle," one senior broker here said.
"It looks like the sign of a change in power... but we know not much news escapes from Mediobanca," another broker said.
Ordinary shares in the powerful merchant bank dipped two percent to 10,190 lire in early trade but recovered to just 0.37 percent down at 10,450 by 1134 GMT in a generally weak market.
Mediobanca, regarded as Italy's most powerful private financial institution, has no media relations office and rarely communicates officially with the press.

Its honorary chairman, Enrico Cuccia, who will be 90 this year, has carved out a strategic role for the bank, controlling significant stakes in major Italian companies through a network of alliances with top business families.
But the press is now questioning whether the powerbroker's strength is waning after it came embarrassingly unstuck in two high-profile merger operations in the past two years.

An attempt in 1995 to marry financial holding Gemina to Ferruzzi Finanziaria and its sister company Montedison in a project dubbed SuperGemina fell through after an accounting probe at one of its subsidiaries.
A second attempt to wed Gemina's textile operations, renamed HPI, to family clothing and textiles group Marzotto early this year collapsed when Marzotto pulled out of the deal.
